did_you_know.text: The kings Rezin of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to wage war against Jerusalem, but they could not conquer it.
The news that Aram had camped in Ephraim caused the hearts of Ahaz and his people to tremble “like the trees of the forest shake before the wind.”
Isaiah was sent to meet Ahaz near the conduit of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Washerman’s Field, accompanied by his son Shear-Jashub.
Isaiah compares Rezin and Pekah to “two smoldering stubs of firewood” and encourages Ahaz to be careful, calm his fears, and not lose heart.
Aram and Ephraim intended to break into Judah and place another king on its throne—namely, the son of Tabeel.
According to the word of the Lord, the plan of Aram and Ephraim against Judah will not succeed.
Isaiah offers Ahaz the opportunity to ask the Lord for a sign—from the depths below or the heights above—that is, to request a sign of extraordinary significance.
Ahaz refuses to ask for a sign, saying that he does not want to test the Lord.
After Ahaz refuses, Isaiah announces that the house of David will receive a sign: a young woman will conceive and give birth to a son, and his name will be Immanuel.

The king of Assyria is portrayed in a striking image as a hired razor that will shave the head, the hair of the legs, and even the beard—an image of the humiliation and destruction he will bring upon the land.
